items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VII, List of Answers on Terminology 54:1
items.html: The lights of Hochma are ordinarily revealed while covered by the posterior of Ima, but only in a thin garment. When they lack even this thin garment, they are exposed too much. The first four kings of Nekudim received the illumination of Hochma with no garment at all from the posterior of Ima, and therefore their breaking was harsh. There are also exposed Hassadim and Gevurot, which is a different matter: as long as there is no illumination of Hochma in Hesed and Gevura, they are regarded as covered by the posterior of Ima, and by this covering they are corrected through the illumination of GAR. But when they have the illumination of Hochma, they are regarded as revealed, outside the covering of Ima, since they then have a standing of their own. (p. 528, Item 49)
